title: Cardiac Muscle Cell-based Actuator and Self-stabilizing Biorobot - Part 2
protocol: Prepare warm DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin antibiotic.
Take T-25 flasks containing the functionalized device (biological actuator or biorobot).
Make a small funnel by rolling a square plastic sheet.
Sterilize the plastic sheet used for the funnel via UV light for at least 30 minutes before use.
Place the funnel over the biological actuator or biorobot inside the T-25 flask.
Adjust the diameter of the wider end of the funnel to fit the entire device and ensure it fits snugly when the top of the flask is tightened.
For biorobots, hold the device in place at the bottom of the flask using a magnet during the seeding process.
Resuspend cardiomyocytes in DMEM complete at a density of 1.6 x 10^7 cells/mL.
Drop 400 µL of cell suspension onto the device through the funnel.
Determine the number of cells obtained using a hemocytometer or other cell counter.
Move the system back into the incubator without disturbing the device and the funnel.
Culture for 24 hours at 37 °C.
Remove the funnel slowly after the incubation period.
Gently wash the sample with PBS.
Refill the flask with 10 mL of fresh DMEM complete.
For biorobots, remove the magnet to float the device.
Prepare materials required for calcium flux assay including calcium fluo-4-acetomethyl (AM) ester and nonionic surfactant polyol.
Gently transfer the device from the culture flask to a 35-mm Petri dish containing 2 mL of Tyrode's salt solution using long tweezers.
Take 1 mL of warm Tyrode's solution (37 °C).
Add 3-5 µL of stock calcium fluo-4 AM dye to the Tyrode's solution.
Add an equal part of nonionic surfactant polyol (0.2%) to the solution.
Replace the sample solution with the warm Tyrode's solution supplemented with fluo-4 and 0.2% nonionic surfactant.
Incubate for 25 - 30 min at 37 °C.
Remove the dye solution from the sample.
Gently wash the sample twice with fresh Tyrode's solution.
Re-incubate the sample in 2 mL of fresh DMEM complete for another 30 min at 37 °C prior to imaging.
Prepare 10% goat serum (GS) in phosphate-buffered saline solution (PBS).
Prepare 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in diH₂O.
Prepare 0.1% cell lyse detergent in PBS.
Dilute primary antibodies (anti-mouse monoclonal antibody cardiac troponin-I and anti-rabbit monoclonal antibody connexins-43).
Dilute secondary antibodies (Alexa 594 conjugate and goat anti-mouse IgG (H+L) Alexa 488 conjugate).
Remove the sample of interest from the flask.
Wash the sample twice with PBS.
Add a droplet of PBS onto a small coverslip.
Gently hold the base of the device with tweezers and cut the thin PDMS arms from the end where it connects to the top of the base.
Transfer the cantilever arms onto the droplet with the cell-adhered side facing upward.
Fix the samples with 4% PFA.
Perform double immunostaining of the samples as described previously.
Mount the samples onto a clean glass slide using anti-fade mounting reagent.
Set aside the mounted samples undisturbed in the dark for 24 h.
Repeat the procedure for all samples.
Manually adjust the lens dial to bring the image into focus.
Select "Crop to region of interest (ROI)" from the top panel.
Draw a rectangle in the video frame enclosing the biological actuator device and cantilever arms to mark the ROI.
Set the frame rate by adjusting the exposure and pixel ratio in the camera settings.
Set the frame rates to about 30 ± 2 fps.
Click the "Record" button to start recording videos of the actuators with a resolution of 1,000 x 1,000 pixels for precisely 30 seconds.
Analyze the images using a programming software (e.g., Matlab).
Run the custom script by opening it from the menu bar at the top.
Ensure that recorded TIFF images are in the same folder as the .m file.
Click "Run" to start the image analysis script.
Press "play" to begin analyzing the TIFF files.
Click the "open" button and locate the TIFF file for analysis.
Click the "base" button, then click on the point where the cantilever attaches to the base at the top; hit enter.
Click the "Scale" button and manually click on one edge of the glass bead.
Bring the mouse pointer to the opposite side of the glass bead and press "Enter."
Click the "Analyze" button.
Click along the cantilever at a short distance from the first square marker representing the cantilever base.
Continue clicking along the cantilever, including the tip, and press enter when done.
Note: The center and diameter of a circle will be calculated using a least squares fitting function.
Check if the superimposed circle correctly traces the cantilever profile.
Click the "next frame" button.
Repeat steps from clicking the "Analyze" button until all frames in the TIFF file have been processed.
Once all frames are processed, click the "Export" button.
Edit the filename to include which side (left or right) of the cantilever was analyzed.
Calculate the surface stress, "σ," on the cantilever using the equation provided.
Open the .xls spreadsheet file.
Calculate the x and y coordinates of each point based on the data in the columns.
Plot the stresses over the time-lapse image frames to observe changes in force exerted on the cantilever over time.
Open the image analysis software (e.g., ImageJ).
Press "File" and "Open" and select the swimming biorobot video file.
Click "OK" and let the program load the file.
Open the spreadsheet software.
In the loaded biorobot video, find a reference of known dimensions (e.g., a 3 mm diameter glass bead embedded in the biological actuator).
Use the "Straight" tool to draw a line across the glass bead.
Click "Analyze" and select "Set scale."
Set the "Known distance" field to "3,000 µm" and click "Ok."
Choose a point on the device that does not wobble between frames to act as a marker (e.g., a corner of the base).
Point to the selected point in 5.1.4 on the first frame.
Record the x and y coordinates on the spreadsheet.
Switch back to the image analysis software window and press the right arrow key to change to the next frame.
Point to the marker again and record the x and y coordinates on the spreadsheet.
Repeat step 5.1.6 for all frames.
Calculate the swimming parameters of the biorobot using the spreadsheet of coordinates.
Calculate the period between frames from the known frame rate of each video.
Calculate the change in the x and y coordinates between frames to find the distance moved, including the total distance.
Calculate the amplitude of contraction from the maximum change along the y-axis.
Determine the beating frequency for each biorobot from the inverse of the period between two contractions.
Calculate the swimming speed of each device from the total time and distance moved in the x-direction.
Repeat step 5.2 for each biorobot video that was analyzed.
Normalize each measured parameter.
Open the image analysis software and select "File" -> "Open" to load the images.
Draw a rectangular polygon on the image frame to mark the ROI.
Select "Analyze" -> "Measure" to measure the mean fluorescent intensity.
Repeat step 6.2 to collect intensity measurements from all the samples.
Calculate the respective mean intensity for each condition.
Export the results on a spreadsheet for further statistical analysis.
Produce data plots using the exported data.
